title: TSMC Eyes Sherman for $120 Billion Chip Expansion
gist: TSMC is reportedly considering Sherman, Texas for an expansion of up to $120B and as many as six fabs (~$20B each); separate state documents show a $45B, two-fab, 5,000-job proposal not publicly tied to TSMC. Only the dispatch of Texas evaluation teams is confirmed by CEO C.C. Wei.

insights.claim: TSMC is reportedly considering Sherman, Texas for a semiconductor expansion of up to $120 billion with as many as six fabs at roughly $20 billion each, which would be one of the largest chip investments in US history.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Would materially expand TSMC's US footprint beyond Arizona; treat as unconfirmed.

insights.claim: Separate Texas state documents describe a $45 billion proposal for two semiconductor plants with 5,000 potential jobs, but they do not publicly identify TSMC.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A concrete paper trail exists, but attribution to TSMC is inference.
insights.quote: A $45 billion proposal involving two semiconductor plants

insights.claim: Sherman is seen as a candidate because of its established semiconductor industry, available land and water infrastructure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Water and land availability are gating factors for US fab siting.
insights.quote: Sherman has emerged as a possible location due to its established semiconductor industry, available land and water infrastructure.

insights.claim: On TSMC's October 15 earnings call, CEO C.C. Wei confirmed only that TSMC sent evaluation teams to Texas to explore manufacturing expansion; TSMC has not confirmed Sherman, the $120 billion figure, or construction plans.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Headline numbers are speculative; position on confirmed Texas exploration, not dollar figures.
insights.quote: However, TSMC has not confirmed Sherman, committed $120 billion or announced construction plans.
